title: Normalized all-degree cohomology of global internal Hom
statement: Use the scalar derived sections and compositors of [def-sfb-space-affine-global-sections] and [def-sfb-space-affine-sections-compositors], and retain their data S,A,Y≅Spec A,X,f. Use the fixed internal Hom and ambient unbounded derived category of [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus], the sheaf Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex], independent-coefficient K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex], and the fixed K-injective replacement and localized Hom comparisons [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]. For cochain complexes P,I define the complex Γ_{X,A}Hom(P,I). After forgetting A-scalars, its canonical comparison with the ordinary morphism Hom complex is the unique chain isomorphism whose (n,p,q)-component, p+n=q, sends a section s to the module map corresponding to its projection s→Hom(P^p,I^q) under Hom(O,Hom(P^p,I^q))=Hom(P^p,I^q). Define the induced additive cohomology comparison using the localization homology-factor isomorphism and the exact forgetful functor's homology comparison. The fixed resolution I(M) is K-injective; Hom(P,I(M)) is K-injective when P is K-flat; the derived-sections complex unit is invertible on all K-injectives. Therefore the localized internal-Hom comparison and that inverse unit identify G_X RHom(QP,QM) with QΓ_{X,A}Hom(P,I(M)). The ordinary Hom-complex cohomology equivalence is the standard map through cocycle classes, shifted homotopy maps, the fully faithful localization into a K-injective target, and the canonical shift comparison. Define c_{L,M,n}:H^n G_X RHom(L,M)≃+Hom_D(L,M\lbrack n\rbrack) to be the unique family natural contravariantly in L and covariantly in M that, for every K-flat P and every M, is the above representative comparison followed by that standard Hom-complex cohomology equivalence and the shifted inverse of QM→QI(M). This normalization specifies the maps in all integer degrees and for every ambient derived object; it imposes no quasi-coherence or boundedness condition. On D(A), define the canonical map H^n RHom_A(K,M)→Hom_{D(A)}(K,M\lbrack n\rbrack) by: a cohomology element determines a map A in degree n to RHom_A(K,M) using projectivity of A and evaluation at 1; identify A in degree n with the tensor unit shifted by -n; tensor this map with K, evaluate using the canonical symmetry and internal-Hom evaluation, and transport from K\lbrack -n\rbrack→M to K→M\lbrack n\rbrack by the shift equivalence. This gives the normalized ordinary-module identification used in the affine trace statement.
